newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wage case ruling not this week - tribunal.
newsitem.headline: Australian wage case ruling not this week - tribunal.

text.p: The Australian Industrial Relations Commission (AIRC) said on Thursday it would not be handing down a ruling on the national "living wage" case during the remainder of the week.
"There's nothing today and it probably won't be coming out tomorrow. As for next week, who knows," an AIRC spokesman told Reuters.
Parties to the case are expected to be given 24 hours advanced warning of the AIRC ruling.
The trade union movement has claimed a rise in all award wage levels of A$20 a week plus 8.75 percent, and then two further A$20 rises over the next two years.

The ACCI has argued the Commission should reject the ACTU claim and begin work on simplification of award classifications. The government, which has sought an A$8 weekly rise, has called the union claim irresponsible and the Reserve Bank has said the case could markedly affect Australia's ability to hold down inflation.
